about: Made-up school-math tutoring dialogues for testing a step-authorship annotation interface. Every problem, step and message was written for this demo. Message text is stored as it would arrive from a chat export (a few messages carry deliberate copy-paste artifacts, listed in 'artifacts'); build_demo.py applies the display cleanup and writes both pages. 'expected' is the intended label for each unit and is not shown on the pages.

units.problem: A club has 7 boys and 3 girls. Three members are picked at random to form a committee. Find the probability that exactly 2 of the 3 are girls.

messages.text: how do i start this one
Start with the favourable committees. There are C(3,2) = 3 ways to choose the two girls.nnHow many ways are there to choose the one boy?
Right. Now count all the possible committees of 3 members.
Correct: the probability is 7/40.

units.artifacts: AI reply 1 has a lost paragraph break ('girls.nnHow'); the display rule turns it back into a blank line.
units.why: AI reply 1 states step 1 (3) before the student does. Steps 2 and 3 and the final 7/40 come from the student first; AI reply 3 only repeats 7/40.

units.problem: In a class of 30 students, 18 play football, 12 play basketball and 5 play both. How many students play neither sport?

messages.text: 18 football, 12 basketball, 5 both, 30 in the class. how many play neither?
You have the givens. Use the formula n(F ∪ B) = n(F) + n(B) − n(F ∩ B) first. What do you get?
I'll try it later
back. the formula is n�n(n�n∪n�n)n = n(F) + n(B) − n(F ∩ B). what do I do with the 5 who play both?
They are counted twice, so subtract them once: n(F ∪ B) = 18 + 12 − 5 = 25. How many students are left?
tamam, şimdi 30 − 25 = 5. sonuç 5 mi?
Yes, 5 students play neither sport.

units.artifacts: The second chat starts with a pasted formula whose letters were lost in the export; it is shown as □(□∪□). The two-question page shows a 'new chat' divider before it.
units.why: AI reply 1 gives only the givens and a formula (a method). After the new-chat divider, AI reply 2 states 25 first. The student gives 5 first, as a tentative question in Turkish ('okay, now 30 − 25 = 5. Is the result 5?').

Test a value first. For x = 0: \(0^2 - 5 \cdot 0 + 6 = 6\), and \(6 \le 0\) is false, so x = 0 is not a solution. What is the sign of $(x-2)(x-3)$ when $x$ lies between the two roots?

messages.text: Find the domain of f(x) = n√n(n�n−n1n)n √(x − 1) + 1/(x − 4)
There are two conditions to check: what is inside the square root, and the denominator. Which values make the square root defined?
the square root needs x − 1 > 0, right?
Almost: zero is allowed under a square root, so x − 1 ≥ 0, which gives x ≥ 1. The denominator cannot be zero, so x ≠ 4. The domain is x ≥ 1 with x ≠ 4, that is [1, 4) ∪ (4, ∞).
oh ok, thanks

units.artifacts: The first message pastes the problem with a per-character copy of √(x − 1) before the plain copy; the cleaner drops the per-character copy.
units.why: The student pastes the problem (givens) and then gives a wrong condition (> instead of ≥). AI reply 1 only names the two conditions. AI reply 2 states both steps and the complete two-part final first.

units.problem: A fair die is rolled twice. Find the probability of getting at least one 6.

messages.text: how do I do at least one 6?
Use the complement. One roll shows no 6 with probability 5/6, so P(at least one 6) = 1 − 5/6 = 1/6.
but there are two rolls. isn't it 5/6 × 5/6 = 25/36, and then 1 − 25/36 = 11/36?
You are right, I forgot the second roll. The probability is 11/36.

units.why: AI reply 1 states step 1 (5/6) first and asserts a wrong final (1/6), so L3 = yes. The student is first with the correct 11/36; a tentative question still counts.
